title: AI Systems
summary: A production ML/LLM platform end to end: data and feature pipelines, training and evaluation, a model registry, online inference with caching and routing, guardrails, and monitoring for drift, quality and cost.

blocks.text: Framing: design the AI platform a company uses to ship features like recommendations, fraud scoring, semantic search and an LLM-powered assistant.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Ingest data, compute features, train and evaluate models, register versions
Serve predictions online (ms) and in batch; serve LLM completions and embeddings
A/B test and roll back models; human feedback capture
Online p99: < 50 ms for classic models; first token < 1 s for LLMs
Reproducibility (data + code + config versioned); training/serving consistency
Cost control per request; safety and privacy (PII) controls

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Classic models are cheap per call but need low-latency feature lookups; LLM calls are expensive, so routing, caching and token budgets matter more than raw QPS.

blocks.caption: Offline loop builds models; online loop serves them; monitoring closes the loop

sections.title: Deep dive: features and training/serving skew

items: Feature store (Feast, Tecton, SageMaker FS): one definition → offline store (warehouse, for training) and online store (Redis/DynamoDB, for serving).
Point-in-time correct joins for training so no future data leaks into labels.
Streaming features (counts in last 5 min) computed in Flink and written to the online store.
Skew: log the exact features used at serving time and train on those logs.

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Training/serving skew is the most common silent ML bug: the model sees differently computed features in production than in training.

items: Pipelines (Kubeflow, Airflow, SageMaker Pipelines): data validation → training → evaluation → registration.
Experiment tracking (MLflow / W&B): params, metrics, artifacts, data version.
Evaluation gates: offline metrics vs current champion, fairness/bias slices, latency budget; for LLMs, eval datasets scored by rules, reference answers, and LLM-as-judge.
Registry stages: staging → canary → production with lineage back to data and code.
Distributed training for large models: data parallel, tensor/pipeline parallel, checkpointing.

head: Pattern
Use
rows: Nightly churn scores written to a table
Continuous batching, KV cache, streaming tokens
Batch requests, cache by content hash

items: Model router: choose model by task, cost and latency (small model first, escalate to large); fallback on errors.
Semantic cache: embed the prompt, return a cached answer for near-duplicate questions (with care for personalization).
Exact cache for embeddings and deterministic calls.
Shadow deploy and canary: route 1% to a new model, compare metrics, then promote.
Input: PII detection/redaction, prompt-injection detection, policy classifiers, max token limits.
Output: toxicity and policy filters, schema validation for structured output, grounding checks (citations must come from retrieved docs).
Rate limits and per-tenant token budgets; audit logs of prompts/responses with retention rules.
Human-in-the-loop for high-risk decisions (credit, medical).

head: Signal
Example
rows: Delayed labels: precision/recall; for LLMs: thumbs up/down, eval sampling, hallucination rate
Latency p99, GPU utilization, queue wait, error rate
Tokens and GPU-seconds per request, per tenant

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Eval gates, canary, auto-rollback on metric drop
Default features / fallback model, cached features
LLM provider outage or rate limit
Isolation of tools, allowlists, output checks
Admission control, smaller models, batch non-urgent work

items.q: How do you A/B test models?
items.a: Assign users to buckets via the gateway, log model version with every prediction, compare business metrics with significance tests.
RAG for fresh, citable knowledge; fine-tune for style, format or narrow skills; often both.

items.q: How do you cut LLM cost?
items.a: Smaller models for easy queries, caching, prompt compression, batching, limit max tokens, distillation.
